title: Je mange, nous mangeons…
en: -er verbs with spelling changes — and aller
intro: Some **-er** verbs change their spelling a little, only to keep the right sound: *nous mangeons, j'achète, je préfère, j'appelle, je paie*. The endings stay regular. And one **-er** verb breaks every rule: **aller**.

cases.label: -ger: nous mangeons
cases.rule: Verbs in **-ger** keep an **e** before **-ons**: *nous mangeons, nous mélangeons* — so the g stays soft (/ʒ/).

cases.label: -cer: nous commençons
cases.rule: Verbs in **-cer** take **ç** before **-ons**: *nous commençons* — so the c stays /s/.

cases.label: e → è: j'achète
cases.rule: **acheter**: the e becomes **è** when the ending is silent: *j'achète, tu achètes, il achète, ils achètent* — but *nous achetons, vous achetez*.

cases.label: é → è: je préfère
cases.rule: **préférer**: the last é becomes **è** when the ending is silent: *je préfère, ils préfèrent* — but *nous préférons*.

cases.label: ll / tt: j'appelle, je jette
cases.rule: **appeler, jeter** double the consonant when the ending is silent: *j'appelle, je jette* — but *nous appelons, nous jetons*.

cases.label: -yer: je paie
cases.rule: Verbs in **-yer** change **y → i** when the ending is silent: *je paie, il nettoie, ils envoient* — but *nous payons*. (**payer** also accepts *je paye*.)

cases.label: the “boot”: je, tu, il, ils change
cases.rule: In all these verbs, only **je, tu, il/elle, ils/elles** change. **nous** and **vous** keep the infinitive's spelling. Drawn in a table, the changing forms make the shape of a boot.

cases.label: aller: je vais, tu vas…
cases.rule: **aller** is completely irregular: *je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont*.

sections.title: 1. -ger verbs: nous mangeons
text: In French, **g** + **o** sounds /ɡ/ (like *go*). To keep the soft /ʒ/ sound of *manger*, add an **e**: **nous mangeons**.

examples.fr: {Nous mélangeons|sp-ger} la farine et les œufs.
examples.en: We mix the flour and the eggs.

sections.title: 2. -cer verbs: nous commençons
text: **c** + **o** sounds /k/. To keep the /s/ sound of *commencer*, write **ç** (c with a cedilla): **nous commençons**.

examples.fr: Le film commence à neuf heures.

sections.title: 3. The boot verbs: acheter → j'achète
text: When the ending is silent (je, tu, il, ils), the last syllable of the stem is stressed and the **e** opens to **è**. With **nous** and **vous**, the ending is pronounced, so nothing changes. The four changing forms make the shape of a boot.

sections.title: 5. Doubling the consonant: appeler, jeter
text: Some verbs show the open **è** sound by doubling the consonant instead: **ll** in *appeler*, **tt** in *jeter*.
sections.tip: You already know this one: *je m'appelle* is **appeler** with a double **l**!

sections.title: 6. -yer verbs: y → i
sections.tip: **payer** is the one exception that also accepts **y**: *je paye* is correct too.

sections.title: 7. aller: the -er verb that breaks the rules
sections.tip: You already know *ça va* (it goes → I'm fine) — that's **aller** too.

mistakes.why: Keep the **e** so the g stays soft.
No accent with **nous / vous** — they're outside the boot.
Double **l** when the ending is silent.
**aller** is irregular: *je vais, tu vas, il va…*

story.title: La fête de Sophie
story.en: Léa and Hugo shop for Sophie's party.

lines.fr: Samedi, Léa et Hugo {vont|sp-aller} au supermarché pour la fête de Sophie.
lines.en: On Saturday, Léa and Hugo go to the supermarket for Sophie's party.

lines.fr: {Nous achetons|sp-boot} des chips, des boissons et un gâteau.
lines.en: We're buying crisps, drinks and a cake.

lines.fr: Non ! {Nous commençons|sp-cer} la fête à sept heures, et {nous mangeons|sp-ger} à huit heures.
lines.en: No! We start the party at seven, and we eat at eight.

lines.fr: À la caisse, Hugo cherche son argent.
lines.en: At the checkout, Hugo looks for his money.

lines.fr: Encore ?! D'accord, {je paie|sp-yer}. Mais {tu nettoies|sp-yer} l'appartement après la fête !
lines.en: Again?! Fine, I'll pay. But you're cleaning the flat after the party!

lines.fr: Le soir, {ils vont|sp-aller} chez Léa et Sophie.
lines.en: In the evening, they go to Léa and Sophie's.

lines.fr: {J'appelle|sp-double} Sophie ? Elle arrive à huit heures.
lines.en: Shall I call Sophie? She's arriving at eight.

lines.fr: Après la fête, Hugo {jette|sp-double} les bouteilles et {nettoie|sp-yer} la cuisine.
lines.en: After the party, Hugo throws out the bottles and cleans the kitchen.

lines.fr: {Nous appelons|sp-boot} ça une fête ? Pour moi, c'est du travail !
lines.en: We call this a party? For me, it's work!

quiz.q: Nous ___ la farine et le sucre.
quiz.en: We mix the flour and the sugar.

quiz.q: In « acheter », which forms take the accent (è)?
quiz.say: j'achète, tu achètes, il achète, ils achètent
